fixed_features.justification: Grounded in source q-130070, q-130071, q-10217 and q-130072; prevents extra reasoning stages at the requested difficulty.

fixed_features.feature: Five radio choices with one correct whole matrix
fixed_features.justification: Every captured answer bank uses this response contract.

fixed_features.feature: Three-row easy samples; swap banks use three columns and scale banks four
fixed_features.justification: These are observed source shapes from q-130070 and q-130071 and keep arithmetic workload stable. This is a bounded subset, not an essential mathematical restriction; omitted source q-10252 replay is separately a failure.

coverage.result: Faithful read-only band-first model selects every batch item under positive easy-band eligibility, with and without captured inventory excluded. Policy/history are not supplied; no exact live next-draw claim.

counterfactuals.change: Hold input entries fixed, change requested swap pair, scale coefficient, addition coefficient, or second sequence coefficient; separately change scaling target row
counterfactuals.expected: Prompt, key and final solution must follow the new operation; old answer must no longer pass when it is a different matrix
counterfactuals.observed: All six controlled relevant changes yield different independently computed results; every option of all before/after records was tested through the native grader. Actual UI renders all 17 counterfactual records.
counterfactuals.justification: Source tutorial assignment operator assigns new values to each element of the specified row; e-4694 and q-130071 identify target roles.

counterfactuals.change: Rename only the matrix in each of five templates
counterfactuals.expected: Prompt and explanation name change while mathematical result and accepted matrix are preserved
counterfactuals.observed: All five renamings preserve independently computed matrices; new UUIDs correctly refer to semantically same choices; native grader and actual UI verified.
counterfactuals.justification: A/M/N/T/U/V/X in source examples are names rather than arithmetic operands.

shortcut_probes.cue: same target row, different scalar bank
shortcut_probes.strategy: Multiply one nonzero target entry by the requested scalar and select the unique matching entry
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Uniform five-choice baseline is 0.2. This successful simplification requires identifying the target row and performing the stated multiplication; proportional-row distractors make one discriminating entry sufficient. It expresses the target arithmetic rather than an incidental label cue.

band-first selection and history exclusions (conditional read-only model)

delivery.result: No sampled easy decision case was removed by rejection/normalization/deduplication. All exact batch records survive. Within eligible easy band the engine selects uniformly; hypothetical histories change available cases as documented.

limitations: Finite tests cannot establish absence of every shortcut.
Stored generation metadata is absent from the captured non-source inventory; no generated identity provenance can be inferred from a question lacking a Math Academy ID.
Actual policy weights, learner histories and future inventory changes were not supplied. Selection conclusions are conditional on positive easy-band weight and usable/fresh candidates.
Source q-10252 lacks key/solution; computed key is supported mathematically. Its complete bank and q-72747 source bank do not replay; see strict failing regression evidence.

Exact batch has only two swaps, both the same row pair. Repeated numerical row swapping remains needed to select the result; this sample alone supports no conclusion about recognizing other row pairs.
